items.title: High Court refuses to extradite Limerick man accused of human trafficking to Greece
items.summary_raw:
The High Court has refused to extradite Jeremiah O’Brien (56) of Rathkeale, Limerick, to Greece where he faces human trafficking charges over the alleged smuggling of 66 people by overcrowded speedboat. His lawyers successfully argued that Greek prison conditions, including severe overcrowding and violence, would breach his rights.

items.title: ‘We stared into an abyss’: the heroes battling to tame France’s ‘megafire’
items.summary_raw:
Exhausted firefighters wage ‘war of attrition’ against blaze that forced 200,000 people from their homes

By noon it is time for a break. The temperature is about 35C, the smell of ash, cinders and burnt wood hang acrid in the air. At tables laid out in the shrinking shade on the desiccated grass and sand outside the sports centre in Le Porge, 200 men and a handful of women have gathered. Firefighters, soldiers, police, gendarmes, officials, first aid teams, foresters and volunteers sit elbow to elbow, plates of sausages, steak and potatoes in front of them.

The village was evacuated just over 14 hours after the “megafire” – as it has become known in France – broke out 6km away last week. The blaze has consumed 42,000 hectares (104,000 acres) of mainly forestland west of Bordeaux. Though finally contained, there are outbreaks every day, pushing to the limit emergency services and the hundreds of amateurs who have come to their aid.

Despite high security fencing topped with razor wire, large groups of migrants have repeatedly attempted to breach or bypass the border in efforts to reach European territory. items.title: India’s monsoon in danger as El Niño predicted to bring hot and dry global conditions, experts warn
items.summary_raw:
El Niño forecast to strengthen from August to October, resulting in higher temperatures and more extreme weather

India’s monsoon is in danger and hotter, drier conditions are forecast across much of the world as a stronger El Niño weather system is taking hold, weather experts have warned.

items.title: Greece: Residents and Holidaymakers Evacuated by Sea From Agios Vasileios Beach in Boeotia
items.summary_raw:
ATHENS - An operation to evacuate residents and holidaymakers from Agios Vasileios beach in Boeotia was underway on Friday as a wildfire that broke out earlier in the morning continued to burn in the area. The evacuation was being coordinated by the Hellenic Coast Guard's Operations Centre to ensure the safe transfer of everyone along the beachfront. Five privately owned vessels, a tugboat and a Fire Service vessel were operating in the area, while a Coast Guard patrol boat and a second Fire Service vessel were en route. The Coast Guard, Fire Service, the Region of Central Greece and the local municipality were coordinating efforts to evacuate anyone still in Agios Vasileios to safety.

The post Greece: Residents and Holidaymakers Evacuated by Sea From Agios Vasileios Beach in Boeotia appeared first on The National Herald.

items.title: Erdogan Advises Lebanon Against Israel Deal
items.summary_raw:
At a meeting in Turkey, Erdogan advised Lebanese President Joseph Aoun against rushing into any agreement with Israel, claiming Israel has no interest in peace with anyone. He urged Aoun to strengthen ties with Syria and to visit Damascus, and offered to deploy Turkish forces to southern Lebanon once UNIFIL's mandate ends.

Reported by Lebanese outlet Al-Akhbar, affiliated with Hezbollah.

items.title: ‘Extremely scary findings’ show climate crisis is supercharging Europe’s wildfire weather
items.summary_raw:
Latest study says global heating has made hot, dry and windy conditions in Spain at least 20 times more likely

The extreme heat and drought stoking huge wildfires in Spain and France were made far more likely by the climate crisis, a scientific analysis has found.

Global heating made hot, dry and windy weather at least 20 times more likely in Spain and twice as likely in France, experts from the World Weather Attribution (WWA) consortium calculated. The finding is the latest to pin the blame for the continent’s sweltering and deadly summer firmly on the heating caused by the burning of oil, gas and coal.

items.title: Iran’s foreign minister presses European counterparts over bases used in US operations
items.summary_raw:
Iran’s foreign minister presses European counterparts over bases used in US operations

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi urged Bulgaria to reconsider its decision to allow the temporary deployment of US military aircraft at Bezmer Air Base, Iranian state media reported on Thursday.

In a phone call with his Bulgarian counterpart, Velislava Petrova-Chamova, Araghchi said Sofia’s approval of a US request to station aircraft at the base in support of military operations amounted to facilitating aggression against Iran.

He described the move as unacceptable and contrary to the traditionally friendly relations between the two countries.

Iran has repeatedly warned that countries allowing their territory to be used for US military operations against it could “face consequences”.

I

Although these aircraft are an earlier variant, they remain highly capable and will reportedly be equipped with Meteor beyond-visual-range air-to-air missiles.  🛫 According to available information, deliveries of the donated aircraft are expected to begin in early 2027, although the timeline could still change.  If completed, the package would represent one of the most significant upgrades to Ukraine’s combat aviation since the start of the war. items.title: US military says no aircraft hit in attempted Iranian attacks
items.summary_raw:
US military says no aircraft hit in attempted Iranian attacks

The US military said on Thursday that no American aircraft had been destroyed or damaged in recent Iranian attacks. It was responding to a claim, which it attributed to Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, that three F-35 jets and three other aircraft had been destroyed.

US Central Command also rejected a report it attributed to Iranian state media that the commercial vessel Nora had breached the US blockade of Iranian ports.

items.title: Families to be moved out of billionaire-owned tower after suffering without air con
items.summary_raw:
Several councils to stop housing tenants in glass-fronted Britannia Point in London, where tenants were earlier told they could not use air con

As the fourth heatwave of the year hit the UK on Wednesday, Benice Bodah and her three teenage sons braced for more scorching temperatures inside their south-west London home. The two-bedroom flat has a built-in air-conditioning unit, but it has worked only intermittently in the almost three years since the family were placed in temporary accommodation at Britannia Point in Colliers Wood. “It has not been easy, but what can we do?” said Bodah, 48.

Several councils have now agreed to stop housing families in emergency accommodation in the glass-fronted block after the Guardian revealed they had been told they couldn’t use the air-conditioning during heatwaves as it had “not been offered as an amenity” for them. The 19-storey building is owned by Criterion Capital, set up by the billionaire property magnate Asif

items.title: IRGC says missiles destroyed three US F-35 jets at Jordan base
items.summary_raw:
IRGC says missiles destroyed three US F-35 jets at Jordan base

Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) says it fired several ballistic missiles at Jordan’s al-Azraq airbase, which hosts US F-35 fighter jets.

The IRGC said the attack targeted a runway and maintenance hangar in response to a US strike on Iran’s Qeshm Island that killed two parents and their child, the Fars news agency reported.

It said the missiles completely destroyed three F-35 aircraft and inflicted “heavy damage” on three others.

The IRGC also said the attack killed several officers and members of the base’s technical and maintenance teams.

items.title: England on track for record heat-related deaths this summer, official data shows
items.summary_raw:
UKHSA estimates 2,877 fatalities during heatwaves in May and June, almost twice that recorded in 2025 season

England is on track to record its highest ever number of heat-related deaths this summer after the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) announced that an estimated 2,877 people had died in the May and June heatwaves.

The record was set in 2022 with 2,985 deaths, and August, traditionally the hottest month, is yet to arrive. The health secretary, Yvette Cooper, said: “My thoughts are with all those who have lost loved ones as a result of the long and intense heatwaves.”

items.title: US awards Lockheed Martin $58.6bn Patriot missile contract
items.summary_raw:
US awards Lockheed Martin $58.6bn Patriot missile contract

The US Army has awarded Lockheed Martin a contract worth up to $58.6bn to expand production of Patriot interceptor missiles, the Reuters news agency reported.

The seven-year agreement will run from the 2026 financial year until 2032 as Washington seeks to rebuild weapons stockpiles depleted by its war on Iran and military support for Ukraine.

The deal replaces a one-year contract worth $4.7bn that the army issued in April. It establishes a long-term procurement programme for PAC-3 Missile Segment Enhancement interceptors, which target aircraft and ballistic and cruise missiles.

items.title: Egypt says drone attack sparked fire on American LNG ships
items.summary_raw:
Egypt says drone attack sparked fire on American LNG ships

Egypt has attributed a fire that damaged two vessels at the Mediterranean port of Damietta to a drone attack, marking its first official account of Wednesday’s incident.

The Egyptian cabinet said preliminary findings showed that a drone caused the 29 July blaze. No group has taken responsibility.

Authorities have opened an investigation into the circumstances of the attack, citing the need to defend Egypt’s national security and interests.

Maritime security company Ambrey said the drone struck a US-owned floating gas storage tanker before flames spread to a second vessel. Officials reported no casualties.

Egypt’s Petroleum Ministry had previously confirmed the fire but did not identify its cause.

items.summary_raw: BIG: A Russian Kh-101 cruise missile is believed to have entered Polish airspace overnight and detonated in an open field near the villages of Targowisko and Tarnawa-Kolonia, about 100 km from the Ukrainian border. items.title: US munition stockpile could impact operations in Iran, senior army leader tells Trump
items.summary_raw:
US munition stockpile could impact operations in Iran, senior army leader tells Trump

The chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff Dan Caine told US President Donald Trump that the situation regarding munitions stockpile could impact military operations in Iran, AP reported citing a US official.

A recent analysis by Washington think tank Center for Strategic and International Studies suggested that the latest war on Iran has drained more of the US army's already diminished stockpiles of Patriot and THAAD interceptors.

The analysis piece suggested that this would put American troops at more risk if the conflict in the region continues.

According to maritime security firm Ambrey, the Marshall Islands-flagged, U.S.-owned floating LNG storage facility was hit by at least one drone while docked at Damietta Port.  🔹 No group has claimed responsibility for the attack, while initial reports indicate no casualties and no damage to the port's infrastructure.  📍 The vessel was reportedly the only target affected during the incident, with port operations remaining intact.  Although the physical damage appears to have been limited, the incident underscores the growing vulnerability of strategic energy assets as regional tensions escalate. items.title: Three firefighters killed on Crete and in mainland Greece as Europe battles wildfires
items.summary_raw:
Repeated heatwaves and strong winds alarm experts, who warn blazes are becoming harder to quell

Three Greek firefighters have died while tackling wildfires on the island of Crete and in the south of the mainland, the Greek fire department has said, as extreme heat hinders efforts to control blazes ravaging southern Europe.

The arc of brutal fires, which runs from the Atlantic coast to the eastern Mediterranean, and from the Scottish Highlands to the south of Spain, has alarmed experts because many of the fires have been out of control and burning close to towns and cities.

items.title: Trump and Netanyahu explored all Iran options including attack, Israeli official says
items.summary_raw:
Trump and Netanyahu explored all Iran options including attack, Israeli official says

US President Donald Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu explored all paths to curb Iran's nuclear project in their meeting this week, including diplomacy, economic pressure and military force, a senior Israeli official said on Wednesday.

Netanyahu did not tell Trump that Israel's preference was for an attack on Iran, the official said in a briefing with reporters on Tuesday.

"In the end, it's his decision," the official said of Trump. Trump has three options, and all three were discussed at length, the official said: "A deal, continuing the blockade and economic pressures, and a massive strike."

items.title: CSIS estimates the US has burned through so much of its air defense stockpile in the Iran war that Patriot inventories are now under 1,000 interceptors and THAAD is down to about 2…
items.summary_raw: CSIS estimates the US has burned through so much of its air defense stockpile in the Iran war that Patriot inventories are now under 1,000 interceptors and THAAD is down to about 250.  Pre-war baselines were roughly 2,330 Patriots and 360 THAADs, meaning more than half of each has been used up.  On top of that, more than 1,000 Tomahawks and 1,100 JASSMs have been fired, along with heavy drawdowns of SM-3, SM-6, and PrSM missiles.  Rebuild timelines are brutal.  Tomahawk, THAAD, and Patriot need 3+ years to return to pre-war levels, with major FY27 Patriot buys not delivering until May 2029.  It leaves a multi-year vulnerability window for any Western Pacific fight with China.  It also constrains transfers to Ukraine and Gulf allies.

items.title: Paros: Next Hours Critical for Full Control of Wildfire, Deputy Mayor Says
items.summary_raw:
PAROS, Greece - The firefighting operation on the Greek island of Paros continued on July 29 with ground forces and two helicopters deployed, as crews battled repeated flare-ups caused by strong winds. According to Charilaos Giourtzidis, deputy mayor for Civil Protection of the Municipality of Paros, wind speeds in the area were as high as 8 Beaufort. Speaking to the Athens-Macedonian News Agency (ANA-MPA), Giourtzidis said ground firefighting forces were currently operating at the scene, supported by two helicopters carrying out continuous water drops. He noted that, despite the challenging weather conditions, the wildfire situation was improved and almost all fronts were showing signs of dying down. However, authorities remain on high alert, as strong winds could trigger new outbreaks or rekindle existing hotspots at any moment.

The post Paros: Next Hours Critical for Full Control of Wildfire, Deputy Mayor Says appeared first on The National Herald.

Speaking after the joint meeting with President of the Republic of Cyprus Nikos Christodoulides and Turkish Cypriot leader Tufan Erhurman in the United Nations buffer zone at Nicosia airport, Guterres said he has the agreement of both sides and the guarantor powers to proceed with a new 5+1 meeting, provided that adequate preparation is undertaken regarding confidence-building, methodology, and substance.

According to LRT, border guards in southeastern Lithuania detected unusual ground vibrations, raising suspicions that an underground passage was being excavated from the Belarusian side.  🔹 Lithuanian officials requested assistance from Polish specialists equipped with underground detection technology. After drilling a test shaft, they discovered a tunnel approximately one meter in diameter at a depth of around 1.5 meters. The passage had not yet reached the Lithuanian side.  📍 Border authorities believe the tunnel was intended to smuggle illegal migrants, noting that similar underground routes originating from Belarus have previously been uncovered in both Lithuania and Poland, where they were used for transporting people and contraband.  The discovery highlights the increasingly sophisticated methods being employed along NATO's eastern frontier. items.summary_raw:
Five years ago, I wrote an open letter asking climate scientists to speak out against fossil fuels. Now governments are in retreat, it is surely time to act

  • France and Spain race to contain huge wildfires before fresh heatwave begins

Such is the astonishing scale of the wildfires burning at the gates of Bordeaux and Madrid, that if they had happened 20 – even 10 – years back, they may well have shocked the world into taking action on the climate crisis. But like the proverbial frog in a pot of slowly heating water, we have become inured; not only to the ever more devastating impacts of climate breakdown, but increasingly to the actions needed to bring global heating to heel.

items.title: Ships stuck in strait of Hormuz pose ‘super-spreader’ biodiversity threat, scientists warn
items.summary_raw:
Biologists say cargo ships stranded in Gulf may carry highly potent invasive species around the world as trade resumes

  • Middle East crisis – live updates

The closure of the strait of Hormuz has created conditions for an extreme global biodiversity threat, with scientists warning that thousands of stranded ships could spread invasive marine species across the world’s oceans once they begin sailing again.

More than 1,500 commercial vessels have been stuck in the Gulf since the strategic waterway closed on 28 February after the outbreak of the US-Israel war on Iran. An international team of marine biologists said that with the stranded ships remaining motionless, their hulls were becoming encrusted with marine life – from microbes and algae to barnacles and other invertebrates – that could hitchhike to ports around the world when trade resumed.

Αυτό που μέχρι πρόσφατα αποτελούσε υποδομή της παγκόσμιας οικονομίας, σήμερα θυμίζει μια σύνθετη σκακιέρα, όπου ένας και μόνο γεωπολιτικός δρών, ελέγχοντας το κατάλληλο γεωγραφικό σημείο, μπορεί να επηρεάσει τις ενεργειακές ροές, τις ασφαλιστικές αγορές, τις διεθνείς θαλάσσιες μεταφορές και τελικά τη λειτουργία της παγκόσμιας οικονομίας και την πολιτική σταθερότητα.

items.title: Visioner 🇺🇸🤝🇺🇦 Fox News host Sean Hannity paid an emotional tribute to President Volodymyr Zelensky during the funeral of Senator Lindsey Graham, highlighting the late senator's un…
items.summary_raw: Visioner 🇺🇸🤝🇺🇦 Fox News host Sean Hannity paid an emotional tribute to President Volodymyr Zelensky during the funeral of Senator Lindsey Graham, highlighting the late senator's unwavering admiration for Ukraine's leader and people.  Addressing Zelensky, Hannity said:  🗣️ "President Zelensky, I know that Lindsey would have been deeply moved and honored that you made this long journey to be here today."  He noted that Senator Graham passed away shortly after returning from another visit to Kyiv, where he had met with the Ukrainian president.  🗣️ "He saw you, and he said it to me once, as a warrior-poet or a warrior-comedian. He used those terms."  Hannity concluded by recalling Graham's profound respect for Ukraine's resistance.  🗣️ "He was proud of you and the courage of your countrymen."  The remarks underscored the close relationship that developed between Lindsey Graham and Ukraine throughout the war. His repeated visits to Kyiv and steadfast support for Ukraine made him one of the most prominent American political voices backing the country's defense against Russian aggression. items.title: Erdogan says Turkey aims to sign energy cooperation deal with Iraq
items.summary_raw:
Erdogan says Turkey aims to sign energy cooperation deal with Iraq

Turkish President Tayyip Erdogan said on Tuesday that Turkey aims to sign a comprehensive energy cooperation deal with Iraq as soon as possible, adding that Iraq had offered to provide the country with one million barrels of oil.

This comes after talks between Erdogan and Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi in Ankara took place amid concerns about global energy shortages resulting from the closure of the Strait of Hormuz.

items.title: Almost 4,000 people evacuated from tourist sites near Bordeaux as wildfires rage in France and Spain
items.summary_raw:
Return of winds and extreme heat threaten firefighters’ attempts to bring blazes under control

Nearly 4,000 people have been evacuated from tourist sites on France’s Atlantic coast as the return of winds and extreme heat jeopardises firefighters’ battles to contain wildfires raging in France and Spain.

The precautionary evacuation order in France, which covers campsites, holiday villages and other tourist accommodation around the resort of Lacanau to the west of Bordeaux, exacerbated a wildfire emergency described by the French president, Emmanuel Macron, as the “toughest” situation the country had dealt with since the second world war.

items.title: It’s time to prosecute climate crimes – with laws that already exist | Aaron Regunberg
items.summary_raw:
Some have called for Nuremberg-style trials against big oil. But there are laws already on the books to describe companies’ conduct

The sky outside is hazy orange, and my five-year-old son is screaming bloody murder. “Sorry, buddy, we have to stay inside,” I say. “It’s not safe to breathe out there.” I had told him we’d be going to the beach today. Something inside me tears a little as I wonder how many promises he’ll see similarly broken in the coming years.

Far too many parents were forced to have some version of this conversation with their children this month, as smoke from record-breaking wildfires poured across the midwest and north-east. Some of them already had to tell their kids that their Fourth of July festivities were canceled because of the lethal heatwave that caused numerous mass casualty events earlier this month.

items.title: Guterres Expresses Strong Commitment to Resolving Cyprus Issue After Meeting with Christodoulides
items.summary_raw:
NICOSIA — United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres expressed his strong commitment to ensuring that a solution to the Cyprus problem can finally be reached, following his meeting on Tuesday with President of the Republic of Cyprus Nikos Christodoulides. “This is a visit of solidarity with the people of Cyprus and to demonstrate my strong commitment to ensuring that we will finally succeed in finding a solution to the Cyprus problem,” Guterres said as he departed the Presidential Palace. “Of course, this depends on the Cypriots themselves, while the guarantor powers also have a role to play, but I will do everything I can to support Greek Cypriots and Turkish Cypriots at this very important moment,” he stressed.

The post Guterres Expresses Strong Commitment to Resolving Cyprus Issue After Meeting with Christodoulides appeared first on The National Herald.

items.summary_raw: OSINTdefender Axios reports that senior Trump administration officials believe sustained economic pressure may ultimately inflict more damage on Iran than an expanded bombing campaign, pointing to growing signs of financial strain inside the country.  According to Axios, U.S. officials cite intelligence indicating Iran is struggling to fund proxy forces, facing gasoline shortages, and under increasing financial pressure from sanctions led by Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent. Officials argue those economic measures, combined with a U.S. naval blockade, could prove more effective over time than additional airstrikes.  Axios also reports Iran continues to seek sanctions relief and access to frozen assets through indirect talks mediated by Oman, Qatar, and Pakistan, while the Trump administration insists any agreement must also address Tehran's remaining nuclear material. The report notes President Trump's decision to pause strikes followed military concerns over air defense interceptor stockpiles but says officials characterize those warnings as a risk assessment rather than the primary driver of the decision. items.title: ‘We have lost everything’: extreme rainfall across Asia brings flash floods and typhoons
items.summary_raw:
From Afghanistan to Taiwan, unprecedented deluge highlights devastating impact of climate breakdown

“It rained for 10 days and 10 nights, non-stop – I’d never seen anything like it,” says Anar Gul, a construction worker who lives in the remote district of Dur Baba in eastern Afghanistan.

The houses in his village are built from stone and mud, which makes them extremely vulnerable to heavy rains. After days of rain, Gul’s kitchen collapsed and his neighbour, Sayed Afsar Sadat, saw a large part of his house completely destroyed. “Rains like this are coming heavier and earlier each year,” says Sadat. “They are destroying the roads and washing away our crops. It’s impacting us directly.”

items.summary_raw: ⚡️ Romanian Ministry of Energy: One of the reactors at the Cernavodă Nuclear Power Plant will be temporarily shut down starting July 28 as a precautionary measure due to low water flow in the Danube River. This measure is preventive and necessary to protect equipment associated with three pumps of the cooling system. Any potential malfunction in one of the pumps would require complex repairs lasting several months and could extend up to a year. Peak consumption this week is estimated at approximately 7,300 megawatts, which is about 700 megawatts less than the peak values recorded in previous weeks due to the holiday period. The estimated volume of domestic production will range between 4,000 and 4,300 megawatts, and the difference needed to cover consumption will be provided through imports under commercial terms. • 18:50 — Romanian Ministry of Energy: The difference in quantities required for consumption will be covered without any risks. (Rasd Akhbar Shehaba)

items.summary_raw: OSINTdefender RT @HM_Int3lligence: Belgian authorities have arrested a woman who was interning at NATO's Supreme Headquarters Allied Powers Europe (SHAPE) in Mons, Belgium, on suspicion of espionage. The woman, a Canadian citizen of Chinese origin, was detained on Friday, and the Belgian Federal Public Prosecutor's Office announced the arrest on Saturday.  Prosecutors suspect that she was spying for a third country and was a member of a criminal organization. Investigators conducted searches at both her home and her workplace at SHAPE. The investigation began when SHAPE's own security services flagged her conduct and reported their concerns to Belgian military intelligence, which subsequently referred the matter to federal prosecutors.  SHAPE is NATO's primary military command in Europe, led by the Supreme Allied Commander Europe, and plays a central role in the alliance's operational planning. A SHAPE spokesperson stated that there is no indication that NATO's or SHAPE's operational readiness, command and control arrangements, or ongoing tasks have been affected, confirming that the headquarters continues to operate normally. items.title: Israel's Gadi Eisenkot on Iran:  Regarding Iran, there is one supreme objective and two other very important objectives. The supreme objective is to remove the approximately 440 ki…
items.summary_raw: Israel's Gadi Eisenkot on Iran:  Regarding Iran, there is one supreme objective and two other very important objectives. The supreme objective is to remove the approximately 440 kilograms of enriched uranium from Iran.  If that is not done, the Iranians can, by their own decision, break out toward a nuclear weapon. What does that mean?  It means deciding to enrich uranium from 60% to 90%. That would require only about 250–300 centrifuges operating for roughly three weeks, and they could reach weapons-grade enrichment (90%) and shock the world with a nuclear explosive capability.  Therefore, this is the central challenge that Israel must address together with the United States.  Unfortunately, despite notable military achievements, there has not been even one millimeter of progress toward this goal.

items.title: The Guardian view on Europe’s wildfires: politics must catch up with the new reality | Editorial
items.summary_raw:
At a time when the quickening pace of global heating has never been clearer, climate policies are being deprioritised

A new and ominous word has entered the vocabulary of firefighters struggling to cope with the vast wildfire sweeping through south-west France. A pyrocumulonimbus is a fire-generated thunderstorm that can whip up winds in unpredictable ways, making the containment of a blaze and assessment of its likely course far more difficult. A known phenomenon in North America and Australia, firefighters believe France is suffering its first in the Bordeaux region, as the country endures the consequences of the third major heatwave of the summer and prepares for a fourth.

items.title: The AHEPA 104th Supreme Convention Kicked off on July 26
items.summary_raw:
PHILADELPHIA – AHEPA's 104th Supreme Convention celebrating America during its 250th Anniversary kicked off on July 26 in Philadelphia. As AHEPA opened for business, it chose its Founders Day to kick off the epic week ahead. On this date in 1922, eight visionary Greek immigrants came together in a fraternal bond to form the Order of AHEPA in Atlanta, Georgia, to combat discrimination, bigotry, and intolerance; and to help Greek immigrants assimilate into the mainstream of American society with an emphasis on education and philanthropy, fostering American patriotism, and practicing good citizenship. Since that initial gathering 104 years ago, AHEPA has helped countless Greek Americans pursue and fulfill the American Dream.

With large areas still burning, damage from national park’s worst blaze could take decades, if not longer, to put right

It is the jewel in the crown of the Highlands, one of Scotland’s most impressive natural landscapes, but 12 days on from the start of an enormous wildfire that is tearing through moorland and forest, the Cairngorms national park is unrecognisable.

Hectares of blackened land were visible as low cloud cleared on Sunday, with smoke billowing into the air from large areas still ablaze. In the evening, the sky glowed an eerie orange.

items.title: Critical Three Days for Cyprus: UN Secretary-General Arrives in Nicosia
items.summary_raw:
NICOSIA – The UN Secretary-General is making a new intervention in the Cyprus issue, hoping to break the diplomatic stalemate and restart negotiations aimed at resolving the long-standing conflict. António Guterres is expected to arrive in Nicosia on Monday evening, July 27 and will hold a series of meetings over the following two days. On Tuesday at 10:00 AM local time, Guterres will meet with President Nikos Christodoulides. At 11:45 AM, he will meet Turkish Cypriot leader Tufan Erhürman in the northern, Turkish-controlled part of Nicosia. That evening, Guterres will host a private dinner with both leaders at the residence of his Special Representative in Cyprus, Hasan Diyan, located near the abandoned Nicosia International Airport in the UN buffer zone.

The post Critical Three Days for Cyprus: UN Secretary-General Arrives in Nicosia appeared first on The National Herald.

items.title: Why Norway and Finland Should Preserve Two of Europe’s Most Important Security Arrangements

Svalbard is a stark archipelago of glaciers and coal mines lying 650 kilometers (403 miles) north of Norway’s North Cape, roughly halfway between the Norwegian mainland and the North Pole. It belongs to Norway but is governed under a 1920 treaty that grants nationals of more than 40 signatory states sweeping economic rights while barring Oslo from constructing naval bases or using the archipelago for “warlike” purposes. Authorities in France are battling to contain a huge wildfire near Bordeaux in the south-west as Spain’s prime minister, Pedro Sánchez, warned Spain and the Iberian peninsula were suffering the effects of the climate emergency.

items.summary_raw: Chinese state media, citing top radar scientist Academician Ben De, claims that Pakistani J-10CE fighter jets used their onboard KLJ-7A AESA radars to detect, track, and shoot down Indian jets at ranges near 200 km during the May 2025 clashes, without relying on AWACS or a networked kill chain.  Gallium nitride modules and low-probability-of-intercept waveforms meant Indian Rafales, MiG-29s, and Su-30MKIs allegedly never got a lock warning before PL-15 missiles hit.  US and French officials have confirmed at least one Rafale and one other Indian jet were downed by J-10s that night.  Source: Sohu

items.title: Maine Democrat Senate Candidate Troy Jackson Voted to Allow Some Minors to Receive Transgender Hormones Without Parental Consent
items.summary_raw:
Troy Jackson, the Maine Democrat nominated to replace Graham Platner in the state’s U.S. Senate race, voted for legislation allowing qualifying 16- and 17-year-olds diagnosed with gender dysphoria to obtain nonsurgical “gender-affirming” hormone therapy without parental consent after a parent or guardian refused to support the treatment.

items.title: The US has burned through roughly a third of its total pre-war stockpile of key precision munitions in Iran War.  Interceptors are the most exposed: up to 80% of THAAD (190–290 of …
items.summary_raw: The US has burned through roughly a third of its total pre-war stockpile of key precision munitions in Iran War.  Interceptors are the most exposed: up to 80% of THAAD (190–290 of 360), more than half of SM-3 (130–250 of 410), and up to 61% of Patriots (1,060–1,430 of 2,330) are gone.  Long-range strike weapons are also depleted at scale, with 1,000+ Tomahawks and 1,100+ JASSMs used, and nearly the entire small PrSM stockpile (40–70 of 90) fired.  Source: ABC, CSIS

items.summary_raw:
Report: Trump paused Iran escalation over Patriot interceptor concerns

US President Donald Trump has, for now, set aside plans to sharply escalate the American military campaign against Iran, with growing concern that a wider war could dangerously deplete the Pentagon's stockpile of Patriot missile interceptors and other air defence munitions in the Middle East, The New York Times reports.

According to the newspaper, Trump discussed the conflict with senior advisers and cabinet officials during a meeting on Friday.

items.summary_raw: Visioner ‼️‼️🇸🇦 The Middle East energy grid has exploded into a fresh spiral of escalation after Iranian-backed Houthis struck a major Saudi Aramco oil refinery in Jizan, sending shockwaves through global energy markets.  The massive Houthi missile strike on the critical Saudi oil facility triggered raging fires, marking a dramatic escalation following a intense sequence of naval blockades, tanker strikes, and retaliatory Saudi airstrikes on the Yemeni port city of Hodeidah. With Saudi Arabia launching immediate counter-strikes across Houthi-controlled territory in Yemen, both sides are now locked in a dangerous, direct military exchange that threatens to engulf regional energy infrastructure.  This direct strike on Saudi oil assets exposes the ultimate fragility of regional energy security when proxy conflicts bleed into sovereign trade assets. By hitting Aramco, the Houthis are attempting to force a lethal economic toll on Riyadh, proving once again that global oil supplies remain painfully vulnerable to asymmetrical missile warfare despite years of regional containment efforts.  See the latest updates with us: @visionergeo tweet

items.title: Mitsotakis to Christodoulides: Greece Fully Supports Your Initiatives for Substantive Resumption of Cyprus Talks
items.summary_raw:
ATHENS - Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis said Greece fully supports the initiatives of Cyprus President Nikos Christodoulides for a substantive resumption of talks on the Cyprus issue, during their meeting at the Maximos Mansion in Athens on Saturday. Mitsotakis referred to the wildfires in Spain and France, noting that they once again highlight the importance of the joint Greek-Cypriot initiative to develop a stronger Civil Protection mechanism at European level. He added that Greece is already contributing two firefighting aircraft to efforts to contain the major fires near Madrid.
